active_directory.howToCount: Count physical and virtual domain controllers that forward security (Directory Service) events to Splunk. Exclude member servers unless they run AD DS.
active_directory.customerQuestion: How many AD domain controllers send Directory Service / Security Channel events to the SIEM?
commonMistakes: Counting every Windows server instead of DCs only
Forgetting RODCs or DR site controllers
Equating user mailboxes with interactive directory users

apm.howToCount: Use the number of distinct services or application names under APM management (one per instrumented app), not every JVM/process replica.
apm.customerQuestion: How many application services are instrumented in your APM (per golden 'service' name)?
commonMistakes: Counting every container replica as a separate app
Omitting non-prod if it forwards to the same index
Ignoring head-based trace sampling that still exports metrics

app_servers.howToCount: Count OS instances whose primary role is hosting middleware or business application runtimes (Java/.NET/app servers), whether VMs or bare metal.
app_servers.customerQuestion: How many dedicated application server hosts generate logs you plan to index?
commonMistakes: Double-counting the same host under Web Servers and App Servers
Counting DB servers as app servers
Excluding passive DR nodes that still emit logs

app_servers_nonprod.howToCount: Same as production application servers but scoped to dev, test, and staging tiers that forward logs to Splunk.
app_servers_nonprod.customerQuestion: How many non-prod application server hosts are in log scope?
commonMistakes: Double-counting hosts already scoped under Web Servers (Non-Production)
Assuming non-prod volume is negligible during release testing

application_event_log.howToCount: Use the same Windows server count as the parent Windows Servers source when Application log collection is enabled; volume scales per enabled channel per server.
application_event_log.customerQuestion: On how many Windows servers will you collect the Application event log?
commonMistakes: Counting desktop endpoints
Assuming all third-party apps write meaningful events by default

asset_cmdb.howToCount: Count distinct CMDB exports, LDAP/AD 'golden' identity lists, or automated inventory integrations that feed Splunk (one pipeline per upstream system).
asset_cmdb.customerQuestion: How many systems of record regularly push asset or identity snapshots into Splunk?
commonMistakes: Counting total CI rows instead of upstream integrations
Treating every SCCM site as a separate source when one aggregator export exists

business_txn.howToCount: Count applications emitting business or payment transaction logs (order, claims, wire, etc.), not every microservice unless each emits txn records.
business_txn.customerQuestion: How many core business applications produce transaction-level logs you will onboard?
commonMistakes: Using order counts as 'application count'
Ignoring batch windows that spike TPS
Mixing debug logs with transaction records

casb.howToCount: Use workforce (or entitled) user count covered by the CASB policy set--same basis as licensing where possible.
casb.customerQuestion: How many users are covered by your CASB / SSE cloud policies?
commonMistakes: Counting SaaS licenses instead of routed user population
Omitting service accounts with API activity
Using global user count when only a BU is enforced

config_mgmt.howToCount: Count servers, VMs, or instances managed by Ansible Tower, Puppet, Chef, Salt, etc., that emit run reports or change events.
config_mgmt.customerQuestion: How many endpoints are managed by your configuration or desired-state automation platform?
commonMistakes: Counting only masters/orchestrators
Including containers twice if also counted elsewhere without scope rules

cspm.howToCount: Count AWS accounts, Azure subscriptions, GCP projects (or folders if one export), OCI tenancies--match the CSPM product's billing boundary.
cspm.customerQuestion: How many cloud accounts or subscriptions does your CSPM continuously assess?
commonMistakes: Counting every resource instead of account boundary
Excluding sandbox accounts that still generate findings
Mixing CSPM with pure CWPP only

cwpp.howToCount: Count servers, VMs, and Kubernetes worker nodes (or pods if licensed per pod) covered by the workload protection product.
cwpp.customerQuestion: How many OS instances or nodes run the cloud workload protection agent?
commonMistakes: Double-counting EDR on same host without dedupe rules
Using hypervisor count instead of VM/agent count

database.howToCount: Count RDBMS/NoSQL instances (one per SID/database service). For Always On clusters, count each replica that independently emits audit logs if forwarded separately.
database.customerQuestion: How many database instances will forward audit or diagnostic logs?
commonMistakes: Counting schemas instead of instances
Ignoring passive replicas with audit enabled
Combining dev/test without scope

db_access.howToCount: Count only database instances where access auditing (logins, object access) is enabled and forwarded--not total enterprise DB inventory.
db_access.customerQuestion: For how many database instances will you collect access or unified audit trails?
commonMistakes: Assuming default auditing is on
Forgetting proxy/scan user noise in logs

db_transaction.howToCount: Count instances emitting redo/binlog/transaction telemetry or verbose statement logs; align with DBA guidance on who runs txn log shipping to the SIEM.
db_transaction.customerQuestion: How many databases produce high-volume transactional or redo-class logs you plan to index?
commonMistakes: Enabling full statement logging without filtering
Underestimating OLTP peak windows

ddos.howToCount: Count contracted DDoS protection services or on-prem appliances that export attack/mitigation logs per site or per service.
ddos.customerQuestion: How many DDoS protection services or scrubbing endpoints feed logs?
commonMistakes: Counting public IPs instead of contracted services
Omitting DNS-based protection logs

deception.howToCount: Count deception agents, honeypot VMs, or appliance-managed decoys that generate security events--exclude production workloads.
deception.customerQuestion: How many deception assets actively generate telemetry to the SIEM?
commonMistakes: Counting production servers as decoys
Ignoring emulated services that burst alerts during scans

desktops.howToCount: Count laptops/desktops with forwarders or agents shipping endpoint logs (physical plus persistent VDI golden images × concurrent if licensing differs).
desktops.customerQuestion: How many employee workstations forward Windows/Linux/macOS security logs?
commonMistakes: Using headcount instead of deployed agents
Counting kiosk/shared devices twice
Omitting contractors with managed devices

devops_cicd.primaryUnit: CI/CD controller hosts or SaaS orgs
devops_cicd.howToCount: Count self-hosted controllers (Jenkins masters, GitLab runners managers) or, for SaaS, count distinct orgs/projects only if each exports separately. Prefer counting systems that emit build audit streams.
devops_cicd.customerQuestion: How many CI/CD systems export build, deploy, and audit events you will ingest?
commonMistakes: Counting every ephemeral build pod as a permanent unit
Ignoring Git audit vs pipeline logs split

dhcp.howToCount: Count DHCP server appliances or OS roles that serve leases and forward DHCP logs.
dhcp.customerQuestion: How many DHCP servers send lease and conflict events to Splunk?
commonMistakes: Counting relays instead of authoritative servers
Mixing IPAM-only exports with DHCP service logs

dhcp_server_logs.howToCount: Use the Windows server count for hosts running the DHCP Server role whose DHCP service logs are collected.
dhcp_server_logs.customerQuestion: How many Windows DHCP servers will forward DHCP server service logs?
commonMistakes: Counting all Windows servers instead of DHCP role holders

dlp.howToCount: Prefer the DLP console's covered-endpoint or covered-user metric; align with policy enforcement scope.
dlp.customerQuestion: How many users or endpoints are actively enforced by DLP policies feeding the SIEM?
commonMistakes: Using email-only DLP stats for endpoint DLP
Omitting server DLP agents

dns.howToCount: Count servers or appliances answering internal DNS that export queries or rpz hits; add resolver clusters as one unit per HA pair if logs are merged.
dns.customerQuestion: How many DNS systems export query or security logs (not just SNMP)?
commonMistakes: Counting external public resolvers you don't operate
Enabling full query logging without sizing

dns_server_logs.howToCount: Count Windows servers running the DNS Server role with analytical/debug logging forwarded.
dns_server_logs.customerQuestion: How many Windows DNS servers forward DNS analytical logs?
commonMistakes: Confusing with generic Windows Security events only

dpi.howToCount: Count inline DPI systems or modules generating metadata/PCAP-derived events; use monitored bandwidth as secondary scaling input.
dpi.customerQuestion: How many DPI systems or taps export events, and what aggregate inspected throughput?
commonMistakes: Equating SPAN ports with production DPI capacity
Ignoring SSL inspection policy impact

edr.howToCount: Count all devices with the EDR agent enrolled (workstations + servers). Use the vendor console's active-sensor count where available.
edr.customerQuestion: How many endpoints report into your EDR platform daily?
commonMistakes: Deduping VDI by image instead of active sessions policy
Counting stale/offline agents
Mixing MDM-only with EDR

email.howToCount: Count SMTP gateways, hybrid Exchange nodes, or logical mail-hygiene services exporting message logs. Use mailbox/user count as secondary for SaaS.
email.customerQuestion: How many mail security hops or Exchange systems forward message tracking and filtering logs?
commonMistakes: Counting every M365 license instead of hybrid servers
Omitting journaling mailboxes
Ignoring TLS report-only appliances

firewalls.howToCount: Each physical appliance, logical HA member (if separately logged), and distinct vFW instance counts as one; cloud FWaaS often per region/policy bundle per vendor guidance.
firewalls.customerQuestion: How many firewall devices or separately logged virtual instances send traffic/threat logs?
commonMistakes: Counting HA passive devices without logs
Treating VPN concentrator logs as separate firewall without scoping
Missing east-west internal firewalls

forwarded_events.howToCount: Count Windows Event Collector servers or endpoints using forwarded subscriptions; ingestion scales with collected source servers, not just collectors.
forwarded_events.customerQuestion: How many servers participate in Windows Event Forwarding collections you index?
commonMistakes: Counting only collectors and ignoring upstream members

fw_internal.howToCount: Subset of total firewalls enforcing east-west policies; count each logged instance separately from perimeter.
fw_internal.customerQuestion: How many internal segmentation firewalls forward logs?
commonMistakes: Double-counting the same device under perimeter and internal

fw_perimeter.howToCount: Count only border firewalls or cloud edge instances directly handling north-south traffic with logging enabled.
fw_perimeter.customerQuestion: How many perimeter firewalls export north-south traffic logs?
commonMistakes: Including internal-only virtual firewalls
Missing cloud edge NGFW pairs per AZ

fw_waf.primaryUnit: WAF instances or protected app pairs
fw_waf.howToCount: Count deployed WAF appliances, cloud WAF instances, or ADC-integrated WAF modules that emit security/access logs per vendor unit of scale.
fw_waf.customerQuestion: How many WAF instances or logical services generate logs you will onboard?
commonMistakes: Counting origin web servers as WAFs
Omitting CDN-managed WAF edges

hypervisor.howToCount: Count ESXi hosts, Hyper-V nodes, KVM hosts, etc., that export hypervisor management/audit logs--not every guest VM.
hypervisor.customerQuestion: How many hypervisor hosts forward host-level audit and task events?
commonMistakes: Counting every VM instead of hosts
Ignoring vCenter-only exports without host logs

iaas.howToCount: Standard mode: count AWS accounts, Azure subscriptions, GCP projects, OCI tenancies, or IBM accounts. Advanced mode: enter scope-specific counts when the customer knows VM, storage, flow log, or Kubernetes details.
iaas.customerQuestion: How many cloud accounts or subscriptions will feed control-plane and security logs? (Use advanced sizing if they can provide VM, flow log, storage, or Kubernetes counts.)
commonMistakes: Using instance count as the primary account metric in standard mode
Double-counting VMs or clusters also sized as separate child sources

iaas_containers.howToCount: Enter cluster count (control-plane and audit), node count (kubelet/runtime/infrastructure logs), and active pods or containers emitting stdout. Use pod count as an approximation if container count is unknown.
iaas_containers.customerQuestion: How many clusters, nodes, and active pods/containers forward platform and application logs?
commonMistakes: Counting namespaces as clusters
Sizing container stdout here and again under application or web server sources
Ignoring managed control plane log settings

secondaryUnits: Collection profile (base vs full VM logs)
iaas_instances.howToCount: Enter the number of cloud VMs or instances sending logs via cloud-native agents (CloudWatch, Azure Monitor, Ops Agent, etc.) or VM log forwarding. Choose base telemetry or full VM logs based on what the agent collects.
iaas_instances.customerQuestion: How many cloud VMs or instances will send logs, and what is the agent collection profile?
commonMistakes: Including stopped instances that are not logging
Sizing application logs here and again under Application Servers or Web Servers
Double-counting with on-prem Linux/Windows server sources for the same workloads

iaas_storage.primaryUnit: Storage assets (buckets, accounts, volumes, or filesystems)
secondaryUnits: Collection profile (base vs full access logs)
iaas_storage.howToCount: For AWS and Google, count buckets. For Azure, count storage accounts. For NetApp, count volumes. For Dell PowerScale, count filesystems or access zones. Choose base telemetry or full access logs based on what is collected.
iaas_storage.customerQuestion: How many storage assets will send logs, and is object/file access logging enabled?
commonMistakes: Counting every bucket when only sensitive prefixes log
Sizing access logs here and again under Application Servers or Web Servers
Double-counting with IaaS advanced storage bucket counts

ics_scada.howToCount: Count HMI/SCADA servers, historians, or OT security monitors representing a plant line or cell--not every physical sensor unless each exports logs.
ics_scada.customerQuestion: How many SCADA or OT systems (or monitored segments) forward security-relevant events?
commonMistakes: IT asset counts as OT
Underestimating historian polling volume

ids_ips.howToCount: Count inline IPS appliances, virtual sensors, or NGFW blades dedicated to IDS/IPS event export.
ids_ips.customerQuestion: How many IDS/IPS sensors generate alert logs to the SIEM?
commonMistakes: Counting passive PCAP taps twice with NDR
Omitting virtual sensors per VLAN

iis_logs.howToCount: Count Windows servers running IIS that forward W3C or custom logs.
iis_logs.customerQuestion: How many IIS servers ship web access and error logs?
commonMistakes: Counting app servers without IIS
Extremely verbose failed-request tracing enabled by default

linux_servers.howToCount: Count production servers with syslog/auditd/agent forwarding enabled.
linux_servers.customerQuestion: How many production Linux servers forward auth and system logs?
commonMistakes: Containers counted as hosts without policy
Omitting AIX/mainframe-adjacent Linux

linux_servers_nonprod.howToCount: Same as production Linux count but scoped to lower environments that still ship logs to Splunk.
linux_servers_nonprod.customerQuestion: How many non-prod Linux servers are in log scope?
commonMistakes: Assuming non-prod is negligible during release spikes

loadbalancer.primaryUnit: Load balancer devices or virtual services
loadbalancer.howToCount: Count ADC/LB appliances or managed LBs (per active unit) exporting access and health logs.
loadbalancer.customerQuestion: How many load balancers send access and health check logs?
commonMistakes: Counting VIPs instead of devices
Omitting GSLB-only appliances

mainframe.howToCount: Count logical partitions or systems emitting SMF/RACF/ syslog forwards--confirm with mainframe ops.
mainframe.customerQuestion: How many mainframe systems or LPARs export security and operations logs?
commonMistakes: Treating DASD count as systems
Underestimating SMF volume

mdm.howToCount: Count smartphones/tablets enrolled in MDM/UEM with compliance and inventory logs flowing to SIEM.
mdm.customerQuestion: How many mobile devices are under MDM management in scope?
commonMistakes: Counting inactive devices
Mixing BYOD privacy-limited telemetry

middleware.howToCount: Count hosts running brokers (IBM MQ, Kafka, Rabbit), app servers, or ESB nodes that emit dedicated middleware logs.
middleware.customerQuestion: How many middleware nodes forward application/integration logs?
commonMistakes: Counting Kafka topics instead of brokers
Double-counting with app_servers

middleware_nonprod.howToCount: Same as production middleware but scoped to lower environments that still ship broker and integration logs to Splunk.
middleware_nonprod.customerQuestion: How many non-prod middleware nodes are in log scope?
commonMistakes: Assuming non-prod brokers are silent
Double-counting shared integration test harnesses

nac.howToCount: Count Cisco ISE PSNs, Aruba ClearPass nodes, or equivalent policy servers exporting authentication and posture events.
nac.customerQuestion: How many NAC policy servers or clusters export RADIUS/posture logs?
commonMistakes: Counting every access switch
Omitting guest workflow logs

ndr.howToCount: Count deployed network sensors/collectors (physical or virtual). Use monitored Gbps as secondary sizing when required.
ndr.customerQuestion: How many NDR sensors cover your monitored network segments?
commonMistakes: Confusing NetFlow exporters with full NDR sensors
Double-counting Corelight + tap on same link without dedupe

netflow.howToCount: Count routers, switches, or firewalls sending NetFlow/IPFIX/sFlow to collectors feeding Splunk.
netflow.customerQuestion: How many devices export NetFlow or IPFIX records?
commonMistakes: Using interface count instead of exporting devices
Ignoring sampler asymmetry across vendors

ot_security.howToCount: Count dedicated OT IDS/visibility appliances (often passive) separate from general IT NDR if split in architecture.
ot_security.customerQuestion: How many OT-specific security sensors forward alerts?
commonMistakes: Mapping 1:1 with every PLC
Missing dual-homed sensors

paas.primaryUnit: Managed PaaS services or app stacks
paas.howToCount: Count distinct managed platform services (function apps, managed DBs, queues) with diagnostic logging on--not every HTTP call.
paas.customerQuestion: How many managed cloud platform services emit logs you will centralize?
commonMistakes: Counting every serverless invocation
Omitting integration with shared diagnostic settings

performance_metrics.howToCount: Use Windows server count for hosts where performance counters are collected at Splunk-relevant intervals.
performance_metrics.customerQuestion: On how many Windows servers will performance metrics be collected at scale?
commonMistakes: Defaulting to 10s intervals without storage planning

pki.howToCount: Count issuing CA servers, online responders, and HSM-attached log sources exporting issuance and OCSP events.
pki.customerQuestion: How many PKI servers forward certificate lifecycle logs?
commonMistakes: Counting public CA certs instead of internal CA systems

powershell_operational.howToCount: Windows servers with Module/Script Block Logging enabled for forwarded Operational channel events.
powershell_operational.customerQuestion: How many servers forward PowerShell operational events?
commonMistakes: Forgetting constrained language mode exceptions
Over-collection on jump hosts

proxy.howToCount: Count explicit proxies, secure web gateways, or cloud SWG connectors with access logs--use protected user count when appliance count is abstracted.
proxy.customerQuestion: How many proxy systems or SWG connectors export web access logs?
commonMistakes: Transparent intercept devices missed
Omitting PAC-based cloud proxies

routers.howToCount: Count managed routers exporting syslog/traps relevant to security--not passive optical gear.
routers.customerQuestion: How many routers send configuration and security syslog?
commonMistakes: Counting L3 switches billed as routers without clarity
Missing SD-WAN edge routers

saas_conferencing.howToCount: Users with Zoom/Teams Webinar licenses etc. covered by audit exports (use admin portal active user count).
saas_conferencing.customerQuestion: How many users are in scope for conferencing SaaS audit logs?
commonMistakes: Meeting minutes vs user seats confusion

saas_crm.howToCount: Enter CRM tenant count, active users, and integrations separately. Choose vendor, collection profile (audit, standard, or full), and activity level.
saas_crm.customerQuestion: How many CRM tenants, active users, and integrations send audit and activity logs to Splunk?
commonMistakes: Sizing Salesforce here and again under SaaS (General)
API integration volume omitted in full-activity profiles
Using licensed seats instead of active CRM users

saas_filesharing.howToCount: Users covered by Box/Dropbox/OneDrive audit logging to SIEM.
saas_filesharing.customerQuestion: How many file-sharing users are monitored?
commonMistakes: External collaborator double count

saas_general.howToCount: Enter actual active users (not per-1,000). Count tenants/orgs/instances and integrations or connected apps separately. Choose audit-only, standard activity, or full activity (including API/integration logs).
saas_general.customerQuestion: How many SaaS tenants, active users, and integrations send logs to Splunk, and what activity profile is collected?
commonMistakes: Using licensed seats instead of regularly active users
Sizing M365/Google here when dedicated Office SaaS child is used
Omitting integration/API client volume in full-activity profiles

saas_office.howToCount: Enter tenant count, active users, mailboxes, file users, and collaboration users separately. Choose Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, or individual workloads (Exchange, SharePoint, Teams).
saas_office.customerQuestion: How many tenants, mailboxes, file users, and Teams users send productivity audit logs to Splunk?
commonMistakes: Counting Microsoft 365 suite and Exchange/SharePoint/Teams workloads twice
Using licensed seats instead of active mailboxes or file users
Omitting shared mailbox volume in Exchange profiles

saas_sso.howToCount: Users authenticating via IdP that exports sign-in logs feeding this bucket.
saas_sso.customerQuestion: How many users authenticate through the IdP whose SaaS SSO logs you centralize?
commonMistakes: Duplicate with Entra ID general logs without scope

sandbox.howToCount: Count malware analysis clusters (physical or cloud) emitting result logs.
sandbox.customerQuestion: How many sandbox systems or services export analysis reports?
commonMistakes: Submission spikes during outbreaks
Omitting integration retries

sap.howToCount: Count SAP application instances or central instances per SID that forward security/audit logs.
sap.customerQuestion: How many SAP systems forward security audit (SM20/SUIM-class) events?
commonMistakes: Dialog users vs named users licensing mismatch

sase.howToCount: Concurrent or provisioned users sending traffic via SASE/SSE fabric--match vendor sizing docs.
sase.customerQuestion: How many users traverse your SASE service daily?
commonMistakes: Site count instead of user count
VPN-only users not hairpinned through SASE

security_event_log.howToCount: Windows servers with Security channel collected; aligns 1:1 with Windows server inventory in scope.
security_event_log.customerQuestion: How many Windows servers forward Security event logs?
commonMistakes: Filtering too aggressively at source losing 4624/4688
Archive-only servers forgotten

setup_event_log.howToCount: Servers with Setup channel enabled--same base count as Windows servers when selected.
setup_event_log.customerQuestion: How many servers collect Setup events (patch/driver install trail)?
commonMistakes: High churn during patch Tuesdays

sso_pam.howToCount: Count unique human identities covered by SSO sign-in and privileged-access logging. Use workforce or contractor identities that authenticate through the in-scope IdP/PAM, not device or mailbox counts.
sso_pam.customerQuestion: How many users authenticate through your SSO and privileged access tooling that forwards audit events?
commonMistakes: Machine accounts dominating counts
Double-counting across Entra and Okta without dedupe

storage_prod.howToCount: Count physical arrays or unified management clusters exporting EMS or audit events, using each vendor's definition of one storage system.
storage_prod.customerQuestion: How many production storage systems forward management and security events?
commonMistakes: Counting individual disks
Ignoring replication partners

switches.howToCount: Count network switches forwarding syslog/traps to SIEM (stack members may count per member if separate streams).
switches.customerQuestion: How many switches export security-relevant syslog?
commonMistakes: Unmanaged access switches omitted
Duplicate stacks

sysmon.howToCount: Servers with Sysmon installed and Operational log forwarded--subset or all Windows servers.
sysmon.customerQuestion: How many Windows systems run Sysmon with events centralized?
commonMistakes: Hashing algorithms exploding EventData size
Over-broad network include filters

system_event_log.howToCount: Windows servers collecting System channel events.
system_event_log.customerQuestion: How many Windows servers forward System event logs?
commonMistakes: Driver noise on legacy hosts

threat_intel.howToCount: Count distinct commercial/open feeds or TIP connectors publishing into Splunk (not raw IoC rows).
threat_intel.customerQuestion: How many threat intelligence feeds or TIP integrations stream into Splunk?
commonMistakes: Treating very large STIX bundles as one feed without volume planning
Duplicate feeds from partner resellers

uba.howToCount: Interactable workforce identities monitored by UEBA product (usually matches HR-active users).
uba.customerQuestion: How many users does your UEBA baseline and analyze?
commonMistakes: Service accounts inflating baselines
Contractors inconsistently onboarded

vpn.howToCount: Count head-end VPN concentrators (physical/virtual) exporting session logs; use peak concurrent users as secondary driver.
vpn.customerQuestion: How many VPN gateways send authentication and tunnel logs?
commonMistakes: SSL portals vs headends confused
ZTNA counted as classic VPN without split

vuln_mgmt.howToCount: Use VM product's managed asset count (servers + network devices + optional workstations).
vuln_mgmt.customerQuestion: How many assets are actively assessed by your vulnerability management platform?
commonMistakes: IP count vs authenticated scan asset count
Duplicates across overlapping scans

web_servers.howToCount: Count HTTP/S servers (Apache, nginx, IIS where categorized here) emitting access logs.
web_servers.customerQuestion: How many web servers forward access/error logs?
commonMistakes: Reverse proxies vs origins
Debug log level

web_servers_nonprod.howToCount: Count HTTP/S servers in dev, test, and staging that forward access and error logs.
web_servers_nonprod.customerQuestion: How many non-prod web servers are in log scope?
commonMistakes: Mixing production traffic through non-prod VIPs
Omitting internal-only staging tiers

windows_defender.customerQuestion: How many Windows servers send Defender operational events?
commonMistakes: Mixing with MDE cloud alerts only path

windows_servers.howToCount: All physical and virtual Windows Server OS instances with forwarders or WEC in scope.
windows_servers.customerQuestion: How many Windows servers centralize event logs?
commonMistakes: Excluding VDIs misclassified
Jump boxes skewing auth volume

wireless.primaryUnit: Wireless access points or WLC-managed clusters
wireless.howToCount: Count APs (or controller clusters if logs are per-WLC) exporting client/session security events.
wireless.customerQuestion: How many access points or controllers forward wireless security logs?
commonMistakes: Autonomous vs controller architectures miscounted
